Lab 1: Getting Started with D3.js

Lab 1: Getting Started with D3.js

CMSC471: Introduction to Information Visualization (Spring 2026)

We will start our journey to explore data visualization! By the end of this lab, you will be able to:

  • Use D3 selections to manipulate DOM elements
  • Create SVG shapes programmatically with D3

Core D3 module to learn: D3 Selection.

Grade (3% of total course grade): This lab is graded out of 30 points. You may submit your lab in person during the lab session on Wednesday, Feb 4, 2026 or Wednesday, Feb 11, 2026, or during any office hours.

The final submission deadline is Thursday, Feb 12, 2026 at 6:00 PM (ET).

Part 1: Setup reminder (10 min)

Required tools

  • A text editor (VS Code recommended)
  • A modern web browser (Chrome recommended)

Local server setup

You’ll need a local server to load external files and avoid CORS issues. You have two options:

  1. Python server:
    • Open your terminal/command prompt
    • Navigate to your project folder: cd path/to/lab1
    • If using Python 3: python -m http.server 8000
    • If using Python 2: python -m SimpleHTTPServer 8000
    • Open your browser and visit: http://localhost:8000
    • To stop the server: Press Ctrl+C in the terminal
  2. VS Code Live Server (highly recommended):
    • Install the “Live Server” extension in VS Code
    • Remember to click on install.
    • Live Server automatically updates the webpage (super convenient!!)

Part 2: Your first D3 code (20 min)

Creating an SVG canvas

In script.js, start with (type in or at least copy them block by block):

Confirm D3 is loaded

console.log('D3 Version:', d3.version);

Create SVG canvas. We select the <div> and append an svg element to it with specific parameters.

const width = 600;
const height = 400;
const r = 50; // radius

const svg = d3.select('#vis')
    .append('svg')
    .attr('width', width)
    .attr('height', height);

Understanding D3 selections:

  • d3.select(): Selects a single element (It’s much like queryselector(), JQuery’s $(), or React.js’s select())
  • Method chaining: Each method returns a selection
  • .attr(): Sets attributes
  • .style(): Sets CSS properties
adding SVG

Wait! There is still nothing? This is because the svg is transparent, but if you use Developer Tools to inspect it, it should be there.

inspecting SVG

We add a border to the svg. You can add this using .attr() or .style(). Here I add a few lines to css/styles.css. #vis svg means that we select the svg nested under #vis.

#vis svg {
    margin: 2rem 0;
    border: 1px solid #ccc; /*otherwise you can't see this part*/
}
SVG with border

Draw with a simple circle

svg.append('circle')
    //center of the circle
    .attr('cx', width/2)
    .attr('cy', height/2)
    // radius of the circle
    .attr('r', r)
    // color of the circle
    .style('fill', 'steelblue');

Note, sometimes you can use attr and style interchangably for SVG elements. But if you setup an attribute with attr you must then use style for editing.

Adding a circle

Part 3: Multiple circles and one rectangle (30 min)

In this part, you’ll create three circles and one square. The shapes will be arranged in a specific way.

Adding three circles

  1. Position the circles at:
    • Left circle: width * 0.25
    • Middle circle: width * 0.5
    • Right circle: width * 0.75
  2. All circles should be vertically centered (height * 0.5)
  3. Each circle should have a different color
  4. All circles should have the same radius

Adding one rectangle (svg.append('rect'))

  1. Position a square above the middle circle
  2. The square should have the same color as the middle circle, and its center is aligned with the middle circle
  3. The square’s width and height should be equal

Rectangle attributes

  • Reference: https://d3-graph-gallery.com/graph/shape.html
  • x and y: Define the top-left corner
  • width and height: Define the size; for a square, make width equal to height
  • To center the rectangle above the circle:
    • x: Subtract half the square width from the circle’s center
    • y: Position above the circle with some padding

Understanding SVG coordinates

  • The origin (0,0) is at the top-left corner
  • X increases from left to right
  • Y increases from top to bottom
  • All positions are relative to the top-left corner
  • Units are in pixels by default
SVG coordinates

Part 4: Data binding (optional)

Tired of copy-and-paste? Or maybe you wrote a loop? We will formally introduce D3’s data binding in the next lab. However, you can try the following code.

// Sample data
const data = [
    {x: width * .25, color: 'orange'},
    {x: width * .5, color: 'steelblue'},
    {x: width * .75, color: '#888888'}
]

// Create circles based on data
svg.selectAll('circle')
    .data(data)
    .join('circle')
    .attr('cx', (d, i) => d.x)
    .attr('cy', height/2)
    .attr('r', d => r)
    .attr('class', 'circle')
    .style('fill', (d, i) => d.color);

Troubleshooting

  1. Nothing shows up?
    • Check console for errors
    • Verify D3 is loaded
    • Check element IDs match
  2. Circles not appearing?
    • Check SVG dimensions
    • Confirm attributes are set correctly
  3. Styles not working?
    • Check CSS file path
    • Verify class names
    • Inspect elements in DevTools
  4. Rectangle not cntered
    • Make sure to subtract half the square’s width from the x position
    • Example: width * 0.5 - squaretwidth/2
  5. Shapes overlapping
    • Check your coordinates calculations
    • Verify the size values
  6. Colors not matching
    • Store colors in variables to ensure consistency
    • Use the same color reference for related shapes
    • Console.log colors to verify values
